# 1 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 3

---

## Council Notes

**On the martial poem (vv.3-9):** The opening hymn to Judas Maccabeus is cast in the style of the hero-songs of Judges and Samuel. The "lion" imagery echoes Genesis 49:9 (Judah as lion) and is deliberate. The poetic register must be elevated.

**On "strength comes from Heaven" (v.19):** All translators preserve this as one of the theological keys of the book. God gives victory, not numbers. This echoes Gideon, Jonathan, and the theology of Holy War throughout the Hebrew Bible.

**On Antiochus and the treasury (vv.28-30):** The parenthetical explanation of Antiochus's financial crisis is the author's implicit theological commentary — the king's own sacrilege is what bankrupted him.

**On Mizpah assembly (vv.44-53):** This is modeled on the assembly at Mizpah in 1 Samuel 7:5-6, where Samuel gathered Israel to pray before battle against the Philistines. The deliberate literary echo should inform the register of the passage.

**Note:** Chapter 3 ends at v.60 in the Greek text. This chapter (like Ch. 4) spans a narrative break mid-action.

---

1. Then his son Judas, who was called Maccabeus, rose up in his place.
2. All his brothers and all who had joined his father gave him their support, and they fought the battles of Israel with gladness.
3. He spread glory wide across his people. He put on a breastplate like a giant, girded on his weapons of war, set battles in order, and shielded his host with his sword.
4. In his deeds he was like a lion, and like a young lion roaring for its prey.
5. He hunted down the lawbreakers and sought them out, and he burned those who troubled his people.
6. The lawless shrank back in fear of him; all the evildoers were thrown into confusion; and deliverance prospered by his hand.
7. He brought grief to many kings and gladness to Jacob with his deeds; his memory is blessed forever.
8. He went through the cities of Judah, destroying the ungodly from among them and turning wrath away from Israel.
9. His fame spread to the ends of the earth, and he rallied those who were perishing.
10. Then Apollonius gathered the Gentiles together with a great and powerful force from Samaria to make war against Israel.
11. When Judas learned of it, he went out to meet him, struck him down, and killed him; many fell slain, and the rest fled.
12. They took the enemy's plunder, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius; with it he fought all his days.
13. When Seron, the commander of the Syrian army, heard that Judas had gathered a company of faithful men — a congregation ready for war —
14. he said: "I will win fame and honor in the kingdom by making war on Judas and his followers who have defied the king's command."
15. A strong force of lawless men came up with him to help him and to take vengeance on the Israelites.
16. As he approached the ascent of Beth-horon, Judas went out to meet him with a small company.
17. When the men saw the army coming against them, they said to Judas: "How can we, so few as we are, fight such a great and powerful multitude? We are exhausted, for we have eaten nothing today."
18. Judas replied: "It is easy for many to be hemmed in by few; and in the sight of Heaven there is no difference between deliverance by many or by few.
19. Victory in war does not depend on the size of the fighting force; strength comes from Heaven.
20. They come against us in great insolence and lawlessness to destroy us, our wives and our children, and to plunder us.
21. But we fight for our lives and our laws.
22. And he himself will crush them before us — so do not be afraid of them."
23. When he had finished speaking, he charged them suddenly, and Seron and his army were routed before him.
24. He pursued them down the descent of Beth-horon to the plain. About eight hundred of their men fell, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
25. Then fear of Judas and his brothers fell upon all the nations around them. His fame reached the king, and all the nations talked of the battles of Judas.
26. When King Antiochus heard these reports, he was filled with rage. He sent out orders and gathered all the forces of his kingdom — an exceedingly strong army.
27. He opened his treasury and gave his forces a year's wages, ordering them to be prepared for any requirement.
28. But he saw that the money in the treasury was exhausted and that the tribute of the region was meager — a consequence of the conflict and ruin he had brought upon the land by abolishing the customs that had been in place from the earliest days.
29. He was afraid he would not have enough — as before — for the expenses and the generous gifts he had been lavishing, since he had spent more freely than the kings before him.
30. He was greatly troubled in soul and resolved to go to Persia, collect tribute from those provinces, and raise a large sum of money.
31. He left Lysias, a distinguished man of royal blood, in charge of the king's affairs from the Euphrates River to the borders of Egypt,
32. and to raise his son Antiochus until he returned.
33. He entrusted to him half the forces and the elephants, gave him full instructions regarding everything he wished done, and especially regarding the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem:
34. he was to send a force against them to crush and uproot the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to blot out their very memory from that place;
35. he was to settle foreigners throughout their whole territory and distribute their land by lot.
36. The king took the remaining forces and departed from Antioch, his royal city, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year. He crossed the Euphrates and advanced into the upper provinces.
37. Lysias chose Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias — powerful men among the king's Friends —
38. and sent with them forty thousand infantry and seven thousand cavalry to go into Judah and devastate it, as the king had commanded.
39. They marched out with all their forces, came and encamped near Emmaus in the coastal plain.
40. When the merchants of the region heard about them, they came to the camp with very large amounts of silver and gold, along with fetters, intending to buy the Israelites as slaves. Forces from Syria and the surrounding lands joined them as well.
41. When Judas and his brothers saw that their situation was growing desperate and that enemy forces were encamped within their territory, and when they heard of the king's commands to destroy and completely annihilate the people,
42. they said to one another: "Let us restore the ruins of our people and fight for our people and our sanctuary."
43. The congregation assembled to prepare for battle and to pray and seek mercy and compassion.
44. Jerusalem lay desolate as a wilderness. None of her children came in or went out. The sanctuary was trampled down; foreigners garrisoned the citadel — it had become a lodging for the Gentiles. Joy had departed from Jacob; the pipe and the harp had fallen silent.
45. They gathered and went to Mizpah, facing Jerusalem, for in former times there had been a place of prayer for Israel at Mizpah.
46. They fasted that day, put on sackcloth, sprinkled ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.
47. They spread out the Torah scrolls — the same ones the Gentiles had consulted to paint the likenesses of their idols.
48. They brought the priestly vestments, the firstfruits, and the tithes; and they brought forward the Nazirites who had completed their vow period.
49. They cried aloud toward Heaven: "What shall we do with these men, and where shall we bring them?
50. Your sanctuary has been trampled down and profaned; your priests are in mourning and humiliation.
51. And see — the Gentiles are assembling against us to destroy us. You know what they intend against us.
52. How will we be able to stand against them, if you do not help us?"
53. Then they sounded the trumpets and cried out loudly.
54. After this, Judas appointed leaders of the people — commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.
55. To those who were building houses, or were betrothed, or were planting a vineyard, or were fearful, he said to return to their homes, according to the Torah.
56. The army moved and camped south of Emmaus.
57. Judas said: "Arm yourselves and be valiant. In the morning be ready to fight these Gentiles who are assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
58. It is better for us to die in battle than to witness the ruin of our nation and the sanctuary.
59. Whatever the will of Heaven may be — so shall it be done."
60. Then Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand picked cavalry, and this force moved out by night
